study_guide.title: Cane Meets the Hurricane Hunters

pages.text: Cane the Weather Dog had a big question. "We can see a hurricane from space," he said. "But how do we find out what it's like inside?" The answer made his ears stand straight up. "There are brave people who fly airplanes right into the hurricane — on purpose! They are the Hurricane Hunters."
pages.ask: Can you believe it? Would you fly a plane into a giant storm?

pages.text: "Their airplanes are big and strong," said Cane. "One team of scientists flies planes named Kermit and Miss Piggy. Another team, the Air Force Hurricane Hunters, flies a plane called the WC-130. A whole crew works together — pilots, a navigator, and weather scientists." The planes fly through the roaring eyewall… all the way into the calm eye… and back out again — over and over.
pages.ask: Remember the eyewall and the eye from last week? Which one has the strongest winds?

pages.text: "Here's the coolest part," said Cane. "As they fly, they drop a little tube of weather tools called a dropsonde." He said it slowly: drop-sond. The dropsonde falls down, down, down through the storm on a tiny parachute. As it falls, it measures the wind, the temperature, and the air pressure, and it radios all that data back to the scientists. "Why do they do something so brave?" Cane asked. "Because a satellite can only see the top of the storm. Only the Hurricane Hunters can measure what's happening inside. Their facts make the forecast much better." "And a better forecast means you get warned earlier," said Cane. "So the Hurricane Hunters gather the facts… and our job is to listen to the warnings and follow our family plan."
pages.ask: Can you float your hand down slowly like a dropsonde falling through the storm?

pages.text: Cane looked up at the sky and smiled. "Thank you, Hurricane Hunters. You're the bravest weather watchers of all!"

study_guide.rule: Hurricane Hunters fly into the storm to measure it — so we get better, earlier warnings.
